open_points.subject: Randomly minted entity identifiers
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns random identifier generation, collision checking and reminting for these five record types?
options: `store` owns one shared minting mechanism used inside record-write transactions
Each record-owning module mints its own identifiers and asks `store` to reject collisions
A separate lower-level randomness/identity module owns minting
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint and collision-check every random record identifier inside the transaction that creates the record.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile M22 creation and record ownership
open_points.text: Two have several, on purpose: StoredValue M21 and value bytes are written by whichever module produces or receives the value ...; NodeExecution M23 is written by `effects` ... and by `runs` ... / The module that writes a StoredValue M21 or a SpooledFile M22 sets its class ... `runs` ... for function outputs ... `effects` for service outputs
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile record owned and created by `store`, by `runs` and `effects` as an additional intentional multi-writer record, or by some other single module?
options: `runs` and `effects` construct SpooledFiles and `store` only persists them
`store.spool_file` constructs every SpooledFile from facts supplied by callers
One higher module owns all SpooledFile creation
open_points.default_guess: Treat SpooledFile as a third explicitly shared record: `runs` and `effects` construct its semantic facts and `store` atomically persists the record and bytes.

open_points.subject: Attempt number used before a NodeExecution exists
open_points.text: `store` alone assigns `attempt_number`, inside the transaction that writes the record, as the ordinal of the element's NodeExecutions (A11 rule 1); no caller passes a number, `effects` included. / A file spooled before its record is written — a function output, a `read` send's file — is named by the element's next ordinal, which the spooling module reads as the count of the element's NodeExecutions plus one
open_points.question: Who determines and reserves the attempt number used to name a file spooled before its NodeExecution: `store` or the spooling caller, and how is the later record guaranteed to use that same number?
options: `store.spool_file` derives and returns/reserves the next ordinal without the caller calculating it
The spooling module calculates and passes the ordinal, contrary to “store alone assigns”
Files use a temporary identity until `store` assigns the NodeExecution number
open_points.default_guess: Make `store.spool_file` derive and reserve the next ordinal from the element identity and require the concluding transaction to consume that reservation.

open_points.subject: Credential non-disclosure after resolution
open_points.text: `installation` ... [owns] resolution of a service credential only when a request to that service is built. / `service_invoker` ... [owns] building one HTTP request ... the credential ... since only it holds the credential at the answer. / The kernel never puts it into the store, a record, a trace, a preview, a failure detail, a log line, a process argument or a response.
open_points.question: Which module owns enforcing the complete no-disclosure rule once `installation` returns the credential to `service_invoker`, especially suppression from logs and unexpected-error paths?
options: `service_invoker` owns all handling and non-logging of the resolved credential until it is discarded
`installation` returns an opaque credential handle so no consumer receives the value directly
`surface` owns a process-wide secret-aware logging and error-sanitization mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Make `service_invoker` the owner of the raw credential's lifetime and prohibit it from passing the value to records, errors or logging, while `surface` continues to sanitize unexpected errors.
